That said, you can't change what she did. What you can do is protect yourself next time. Most honest customers will simply say "I dropped it." If someone refuses to provide that detail, you'll know to treat the claim with caution.

It's also worth checking whether your payment processor or any buyer protection scheme covers "item not as described" differently from "accidental damage." If you can, make your refund policy clear: refunds for damaged goods require evidence, and accidental damage isn't covered. That won't stop a dishonest customer, but it will stop the easy ones, and it will make you feel less gutted when it happens.
